headline: Putin agrees to resume talks on Ukraine war with Kyiv and Washington
standfirst: US special envoy Steve Witkoff discussed a resumption of peace talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine followed by a possible summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping next month, according to Russian…
body_markdown:
US special envoy Steve Witkoff discussed a resumption of peace talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine followed by a possible summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping next month, according to Russian officials. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said after the Wednesday meeting in St Petersburg between Witkoff and Putin that establishing a “security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends” was the main issue Moscow was ready to negotiate on, Russian news agency Interfax reported. Witkoff’s trip, his ninth visit to Russia, is part of a pivot towards Putin in the US’s push to end Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine that has alarmed Kyiv and its European allies. (The Irish Times)

**France 24 Europe** adds: President ⁠Volodymyr Zelenskiy ​said on Wednesday ​that Ukraine supported a US proposal for ​three-way talks ‌with Russia ⁠and the United ‌States at the level ⁠of negotiators to be held as soon ​as possible, preferably ‌no later than early November. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House, says that "it's not clear whether Putin would meet Trump and Zelensky", adding that "meeting Zelensky is the last thing that Putin would be prepared to do".

**Ukrinform** adds: Yuri Ushakov, an aide to the Russian President, has said that trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine could resume in early November.

**BBC News Europe** adds: The announcement came after Russian President Vladimir Putin met US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.

**Dawn** adds: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump called upon Ukraine on Tuesday to make a deal to settle the war with Russia, saying Moscow wanted to end the conflict. “Ukraine has to want to settle this war,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by Hindustan Times, France 24 Europe, The Irish Times, The Hindu, BBC News Europe, Global News, Ukrinform and Dawn. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
